title: Comparisons with and products by power-of-two literals split a double exactly
verdict: native: the split of `_exact_sum._split` is `frexp`'s on every double tested
description: The exact limbs of a maintained double aggregate (#1447) split each finite double `x` into a grid position `p` and an integer mantissa `m` with `x = m · 2^(p - 1074)`. Substrait has no `frexp`, and Spark's lowering refuses `POWER` (`Math.pow`, within 1 ulp), so the split scales `|x|` into `[1, 2)` with comparisons and products by power-of-two literals: a value below `2^-50` goes up by `2^537 · 2^537`, one below 1 by `2^52`, into `[1, 2^1024)`; then eleven steps compare `a` with `2^(2^b)` (b from 10 to 0; `a · 0.5` with `2^1023` for b = 10) and scale it by `2^-(2^b)` where it is at or above. A subnormal's mantissa is its scaled value, the others' `a · 2^52`, cast to `BIGINT`.

On Spark 4.3.0 the plan's result equals `frexp`'s for every `2^k` (k from -1074 to 1023) and its predecessor `2^k - ulp`, 5e-324, the largest subnormal, the smallest normal, the largest double, 2,000 random values across the exponent range, all with both signs: the comparisons and products are exact and Catalyst folds none of the paired literals into an infinity. Zero, NaN and the infinities give mantissa 0.
The plan's row check (an integer mantissa below `2^53`, at least `2^52` for a normal value) checks the normal form only; the give-back rests on this fact (ruling 174, S2).
reference: D25/D30's exact moments (`LinearAgg.no_drift`); `docs/trusted-base.md` lists the split as trusted, with this fact and `test_the_split_is_frexp` as its evidence.

provenance.notes: Run locally: pyspark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.13, macOS arm64, `local[2]`, the session of `sverify_spark.engine.session` (ANSI on). The same test passes on DuckDB and Polars. An earlier run of the split on 48,280 values (20,000 random) gave no mismatch on the three engines.
